claims.title: Illyrian and Greek Butrint
claims.summary: Illyrian tribes inhabited the eastern Adriatic coast, where Greek colonists from about the eighth century BCE helped develop the settlement of Buthrotum (Butrint) into a flourishing city.

sources.label: Albania: Medieval Culture and Illyrian Tribes

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-800bce-illyrian-and-greek-butrint, claim TL:ALB:event:800bce:illyrian-and-greek-butrint, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Roman conquest of Illyria
claims.summary: Rome conquered the Illyrians in the second century BCE and absorbed their lands; Butrint flourished under Roman rule with a forum, aqueduct and public buildings.

sources.label: Albania: Medieval Culture and Illyrian Tribes

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-167bce-roman-conquest-of-illyria, claim TL:ALB:event:167bce:roman-conquest-of-illyria, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Byzantine rule begins
claims.summary: After the division of the Roman Empire the Albanian lands passed to the Byzantine Empire, remaining a contested Christian borderland for much of the following eight centuries.

sources.label: Albania: Medieval Culture and Illyrian Tribes

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-395-byzantine-rule-begins, claim TL:ALB:event:395:byzantine-rule-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Early Christian Butrint
claims.summary: Butrint became an episcopal seat with an early Christian basilica and a baptistery whose mosaic floor survives, marking the spread of Christianity in the region under Byzantium.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-550-early-christian-butrint, claim TL:ALB:event:550:early-christian-butrint, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman invasion of Albania
claims.summary: The Ottoman Turks invaded Albania in 1388 and, over the following decades, brought most of the divided and contested country under their control, largely completing the conquest by about 1430.

sources.label: Albania: Medieval Culture and Illyrian Tribes

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1388-ottoman-invasion-of-albania, claim TL:ALB:event:1388:ottoman-invasion-of-albania, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Skanderbeg's revolt and the return to Kruje
claims.summary: Gjergj Kastrioti (Skanderbeg) broke with the Ottomans after 1443, reconverted to Christianity and seized his ancestral fortress of Kruje, launching a national revolt against Ottoman rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1443-skanderbeg-s-revolt-and-the-return-to-kruje, claim TL:ALB:event:1443:skanderbeg-s-revolt-and-the-return-to-kruje, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: League of Lezhe
claims.summary: Skanderbeg united Albanian princes in the League of Lezhe to coordinate resistance, giving the scattered lordships a measure of common purpose against the Ottoman Empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1444-league-of-lezhe, claim TL:ALB:event:1444:league-of-lezhe, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The sieges of Kruje
claims.summary: From his stronghold at Kruje Skanderbeg withstood repeated Ottoman sieges, including those of 1450 and 1466-67, keeping much of Albania free for some twenty-five years.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1450-the-sieges-of-kruje, claim TL:ALB:event:1450:the-sieges-of-kruje, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Skanderbeg
claims.summary: Skanderbeg died at Lezhe in 1468; without his leadership Albanian resistance collapsed, and the Ottomans took Kruje in 1478 and Shkoder in 1479, completing the conquest.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1468-death-of-skanderbeg, claim TL:ALB:event:1468:death-of-skanderbeg, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Albania within the Ottoman Empire
claims.summary: Following the fall of Kruje and Shkoder, Albania was incorporated into the Ottoman Empire, beginning nearly five centuries of rule during which most Albanians converted to Islam.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1479-albania-within-the-ottoman-empire, claim TL:ALB:event:1479:albania-within-the-ottoman-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman towns of Berat and Gjirokastra
claims.summary: The towns of Berat and Gjirokastra developed the distinctive Ottoman-era urban architecture, including fortified citadels and tall stone houses, that later earned them UNESCO World Heritage status.

sources.label: Historic Centres of Berat and Gjirokastra

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1812-ottoman-towns-of-berat-and-gjirokastra, claim TL:ALB:event:1812:ottoman-towns-of-berat-and-gjirokastra, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Rilindja national awakening
claims.summary: A cultural and political revival, the Rilindja, promoted the Albanian language, literature and a distinct national identity, led by writers and patriots such as the poet Naim Frasheri.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1844-the-rilindja-national-awakening, claim TL:ALB:event:1844:the-rilindja-national-awakening, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: League of Prizren
claims.summary: Founded at Prizren in response to the Congress of Berlin, the Albanian League sought to unify the Albanian lands into one autonomous unit and to resist their partition among neighbouring states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1878-league-of-prizren, claim TL:ALB:event:1878:league-of-prizren, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Declaration of independence at Vlore
claims.summary: An assembly at Vlore led by Ismail Qemali proclaimed Albania an independent state and raised the national flag, breaking from the Ottoman Empire during the First Balkan War.

sources.label: Ismail Qemali Leads Albania to Independence, November 1912

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1912-declaration-of-independence-at-vlore, claim TL:ALB:event:1912:declaration-of-independence-at-vlore, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conference of London and the borders
claims.summary: The Great Powers recognised an autonomous Albania but, pressed by its neighbours, drew borders leaving about half the Albanian-populated lands, including Kosovo, outside the state, creating the Albanian national question.

sources.label: Ismail Qemali Leads Albania to Independence, November 1912

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1913-conference-of-london-and-the-borders, claim TL:ALB:event:1913:conference-of-london-and-the-borders, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The rise of Zog
claims.summary: Ahmed Zogu consolidated power, becoming president in 1925 and in 1928 proclaiming himself King Zog I, ruling an authoritarian monarchy increasingly dependent on Fascist Italy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1925-the-rise-of-zog, claim TL:ALB:event:1925:the-rise-of-zog, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Italian invasion of Albania
claims.summary: Fascist Italy invaded Albania on 7 April 1939; King Zog fled into exile and the Italian king Victor Emmanuel III was proclaimed king of Albania, ending its independence.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Albania
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1939-italian-invasion-of-albania, claim TL:ALB:event:1939:italian-invasion-of-albania, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Communist victory and Hoxha in power
claims.summary: As German forces withdrew, the communist-led partisans took Tirana and formed a provisional government under Enver Hoxha, who would rule Albania for over four decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1944-communist-victory-and-hoxha-in-power, claim TL:ALB:event:1944:communist-victory-and-hoxha-in-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Breaks with Yugoslavia and the USSR
claims.summary: Hoxha broke with Tito's Yugoslavia in 1948 and allied with the Soviet Union, then ruptured with Moscow in 1961 over de-Stalinisation, turning instead to Maoist China.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1948-breaks-with-yugoslavia-and-the-ussr, claim TL:ALB:event:1948:breaks-with-yugoslavia-and-the-ussr, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Albania declared an atheist state
claims.summary: The Hoxha regime launched a campaign against religion, closing mosques and churches and proclaiming Albania the world's first officially atheist state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1967-albania-declared-an-atheist-state, claim TL:ALB:event:1967:albania-declared-an-atheist-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rupture with China and total isolation
claims.summary: Hoxha broke with post-Maoist China in the late 1970s, leaving Albania almost completely isolated, its borders sealed and its economy self-reliant by decree.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1978-rupture-with-china-and-total-isolation, claim TL:ALB:event:1978:rupture-with-china-and-total-isolation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Enver Hoxha
claims.summary: Hoxha died in 1985 after ruling for over forty years, leaving the most tightly controlled society in Europe to his successor Ramiz Alia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1985-death-of-enver-hoxha, claim TL:ALB:event:1985:death-of-enver-hoxha, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: End of one-party rule
claims.summary: After the Tirana student protests of December 1990, Albania held its first multiparty elections in March 1991, and the Party of Labour's monopoly on power ended with the 1992 elections.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1991-end-of-one-party-rule, claim TL:ALB:event:1991:end-of-one-party-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: US-Albania relations resumed
claims.summary: The United States and Albania resumed diplomatic relations on 15 March 1991 after a break of more than half a century dating to the Italian takeover of 1939.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Albania
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1991-us-albania-relations-resumed, claim TL:ALB:event:1991:us-albania-relations-resumed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Pyramid scheme collapse and unrest
claims.summary: The collapse of fraudulent pyramid investment schemes in early 1997 wiped out the savings of many Albanians and triggered armed unrest that brought the state close to anarchy before order was restored.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-1997-pyramid-scheme-collapse-and-unrest, claim TL:ALB:event:1997:pyramid-scheme-collapse-and-unrest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kosovo declares independence
claims.summary: Kosovo, whose population is overwhelmingly ethnic Albanian and which was left outside Albania in 1913, declared independence on 17 February 2008, recognised the next day by the United States.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Kosovo
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-2008-kosovo-declares-independence, claim TL:ALB:event:2008:kosovo-declares-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Albania joins NATO
claims.summary: Albania, with Croatia, formally joined NATO on 1 April 2009 as the alliance's 27th and 28th members, completing its strategic reorientation toward the West.

sources.label: Ceremony marks the accession of Albania and Croatia to NATO
NATO Enlargement: Albania, Croatia, and Possible Future Candidates

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-2009-albania-joins-nato, claim TL:ALB:event:2009:albania-joins-nato, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: EU candidate status
claims.summary: Albania, which applied for membership in April 2009, was granted European Union candidate status in June 2014; accession negotiations were formally opened in July 2022.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Albania: From Illyrian tribes and Skanderbeg's mountain resistance to a small Balkan state forged on the edge of empires.", terralore.co/country/ALB/chronicle#ev-2014-eu-candidate-status, claim TL:ALB:event:2014:eu-candidate-status, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
